newsitem.title: USA: USDA seeks poultry product inspection rules change.
newsitem.headline: USDA seeks poultry product inspection rules change.

text.p: The U.S. Agriculture Department Friday proposed amending poultry product inspection rules to let manufacturers interchange the amounts and kinds of poultry in their products without needing new labels.

In a notice in the Federal Register, USDA said the provision would apply to products where two kinds of poultry made up at least 70 percent of the poultry ingredients used and neither of the two kinds were less than 30 percent of the poultry ingredients used.
Manufacturers would be obliged to use "and" on the ingredients list instead of a comma so consumers knew that the order of the two types of poultry might be alternate.
USDA said it was acting in response to a petition. Federal meat inspection regulations have a similiar rule in place.
The department said the deadline for comments is Feb. 25.
